comparator.name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics
comparator.route: Thematic Package 1: Challenges to the Welfare State; first-listed advanced options Topics in Philosophy and Advanced Disciplinary Course in History
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026-2027 EER and curriculum page establish a 135-EC major plus 45 EC of genuine free choice. The major contains eight compulsory basic courses (60 EC), three compulsory research-methods courses (22.5 EC), one thematic package (22.5 EC), two advanced disciplinary/transdisciplinary courses (15 EC), and a 15-EC thesis. The generic target names no package. The four packages are equally formal and equally sized, and none is designated as the general route; the official-order tie-break therefore selects the first-listed package, Challenges to the Welfare State. The first-listed advanced options are likewise selected neutrally: Topics in Philosophy for the advanced-disciplinary slot and Advanced Disciplinary Course in History for the advanced-disciplinary/transdisciplinary slot. The third methods course and both advanced courses carry official working/TBD titles because they are scheduled for 2027-2028 in the EER for the 2026 cohort. No content is invented for the 45-EC free-choice space.

routeSelection.route: Thematic Package 1: Challenges to the Welfare State; first-listed advanced options Topics in Philosophy and Advanced Disciplinary Course in History
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic PPE bachelor and does not name one of the four equally sized thematic packages. All four integrate the programme's disciplines around a substantive problem, and current official evidence does not designate one as broader or less specialised. The current EER lists Challenges to the Welfare State first, so official order selects it independently of UCR fit. The same neutral rule selects the first-listed advanced options, Topics in Philosophy and Advanced Disciplinary Course in History.

core: Integrated philosophy, politics, economics and history for analysing political and economic institutions
Ethics, political philosophy, justice and public-policy evaluation
Democracy, political institutions, policymaking and pressures on liberal democracy
Microeconomics, macroeconomics, markets and economic-policy reasoning
Global economic history and the historical development of political and economic institutions
Welfare states, social protection, redistribution and the balance between support, responsibility and freedom
Qualitative, quantitative and critical-reasoning methods for interdisciplinary PPE research
Independent interdisciplinary research culminating in a PPE bachelor thesis
adjacent: Markets, regulators, capitalism and relations among government, institutions and business
Sustainability policy, environmental governance, biodiversity and natural-resource scarcity
International governance, conflict, rights and public accountability
questions: How should welfare, markets and public policy balance justice, freedom, responsibility and social protection?
How can political and economic institutions govern sustainability and environmental limits fairly?
How does history help explain current political and economic problems and institutional choices?

alternatives.label: PPE & History: Ethics, Welfare and Public Choice
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates philosophy, politics and economics with two substantial history courses, then applies those foundations to welfare, rights, public economics and public choice.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response integrates philosophy, political institutions, economics and history with research methods, law, welfare-state questions and public choice. It mirrors Utrecht PPE's four-discipline identity and selected welfare-state package while acknowledging that UCR does not offer Utrecht's integrated thematic package or PPE thesis.
progression: Economics and mathematics gateways plus introductory philosophy and politics precede advanced economics, philosophy, history, law and research. All formal prerequisites and term offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Markets, Regulation & Global Governance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres political economy, comparative and international institutions, law, economic methods and the historical development of governance.
alternatives.concept: Develops Utrecht's Markets and Regulators direction through economics, comparative and international politics, public and constitutional law, historical institutional development and quantitative methods. It asks how governments, markets and businesses shape one another without claiming to reproduce Utrecht's integrated package.
progression: No UCR course in this alternative carries a formal prerequisite except the courses that require BENGATE102 (BENECON211, BENECON212, BENECON311, BENECON312, BENECON314), DISGATE102 (DISMATH314, DISMATH211) and GOSGATE102 (GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213); BENGATE102 and DISGATE102 are scheduled in semester 2, and GOSGATE102 in semester 3, each before every course that depends on it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses are concentrated in semester 1, and level-3 advanced work (European Union Politics, Peace & Conflict, Public Economics, Econometrics, Behavioral Economics) is concentrated in semesters 4-6. Where an advisory continuation exists, it is honoured: Foundations of Comparative Politics (semester 1) precedes the more advanced Theory of International Relations (semester 2), European Union Politics (semester 5) and Peace & Conflict (semester 6); Law, Society & Justice (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Introduction to Public International Law and Comparative Constitutional Law (semester 4), both of which formally require it; and Mathematical Methods (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Linear Algebra (semester 3). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the closest curriculum, this route replaces its philosophy, ethics and welfare-oriented sociology cluster with international relations, public and constitutional law, political history, peace and conflict, and additional formal mathematics. Eleven courses differ, shifting the organizing question from welfare and public choice to market regulation and global governance.
traceOverrides: trains formal logic and discrete mathematics for decision-making, directly implementing PPE's own learning outcome of applying formal logic, statistics and decision theory

alternatives.label: Sustainability Policy & Environmental Governance
alternatives.concept: Develops Utrecht's Global Pathways to a Sustainable Future direction through sustainability science, climate and environmental evidence, economics, law, political institutions, justice and public communication. The plan preserves a PPE-style governance focus while adding the environmental knowledge required to evaluate policy choices.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum joins PPE's politics, economics, law and justice perspectives to climate, environmental science, data and applied sustainability research.
progression: Sustainability, law, politics, economics, research and data foundations precede international law, public economics, advanced EU politics, governance, conflict analysis and applied sustainability research; prerequisites and term offerings pass.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most of the closest curriculum's philosophy, history and welfare-state emphasis, and most of the markets route's international-history and formal-mathematics emphasis, with sustainability foundations, climate and environmental science, data, applied sustainability research and climate communication. It differs from each earlier curriculum by well over 30 EC.

selection.assessment: The ethics-welfare-public-choice curriculum is the closest feasible response to Utrecht's four-discipline core and selected welfare-state package. The next official packages support distinct markets/regulation and sustainability-governance curricula. All three are coherent, mechanically feasible and pairwise exceed the 30-EC distinctness floor, so production stops at three.

notes.text: Utrecht PPE integrates philosophy, politics, economics and history through a compulsory common core, an interdisciplinary thematic package, a dedicated methods sequence and a PPE thesis. UCR can construct strong combinations across these fields and related sustainability study, but it does not reproduce Utrecht's integrated package or programme-specific thesis structure.
